messages.content:
You plan the work for one part of a course assignment or project. A team of AI agents will carry
it out: a coding agent builds, a testing agent tests. Design, documentation and the final review are planned
separately, so do not add those steps.

Return JSON with "steps", "research_questions", "not_plannable" and "open_questions".

Each step:
- key: a short local name ("b1", "b2" for build steps, "t1", "t2" for test steps).
- title: an imperative title of at most 8 words ("Broadcast messages to all clients").
- description: one or two sentences on what to do.
- phase: "implement" (build something) or "test" (check that it works).
- requirement_ids: the ids of the requirements the step delivers or checks. Use only ids from the list.
- acceptance_criteria: 1-4 concrete, checkable statements taken from the requirements, keeping their numbers
  ("at least 10 clients connected at the same time").
- effort_hours: a rough estimate for one student (0.5 to 16).
- depends_on: keys of steps in your answer whose result this step needs (a test needs what it tests; the client
  may need the server's protocol). Never depend on a later step in a circle.
- group: a 1-3 word feature name shared by related steps ("Messaging").

Rules:
- Every requirement id in the list must appear in at least one step, unless it is in not_plannable.
- Use as few steps as the work needs: a build step covers 1-4 closely related requirements that one person would
  build together; a test step checks one feature group (it may check several build steps).
- Quality requirements (speed, robustness, usability) usually belong to test steps.
- Writing tests, scripts or documents that a requirement asks for is a build step.
- Dependencies: a step that uses, extends, tests or describes what another step makes depends on it (the command-line
  interface needs the logic it calls; unit tests need the code they test; code implementing a model needs the model).
- At most 12 steps. Never invent requirements, numbers, tools or extra features.
- research_questions: 2-5 specific questions the team must answer before designing (techniques, libraries the
  constraints allow, known pitfalls).
- not_plannable: requirements an AI agent cannot carry out (a live demo, handing in on a portal), with a reason.
- open_questions: anything unclear or contradictory (an empty list if nothing is).

Project kind: software.
Part: Part B.

Requirements:
R3 [must, functional] Implement endpoints to create, list and cancel bookings. (section: Part B: REST API)
R4 [must, functional] Every endpoint must return JSON and proper HTTP status codes. (section: Part B: REST API)
R5 [must, functional] Protect the endpoints with token authentication. (section: Part B: REST API)
R6 [must, functional] Use the schema from Part A. (section: Part B: REST API)

response.text:
{
  "steps": [
    {
      "key": "b1",
      "title": "Implement booking endpoints",
      "description": "Create REST endpoints for creating, listing, and canceling bookings using the schema from Part A.",
      "phase": "implement",
      "requirement_ids": ["R3", "R6"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Create endpoint returns 201 and booking data in JSON",
        "List endpoint returns 200 and an array of bookings in JSON",
        "Cancel endpoint returns 204 on successful deletion"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 6,
      "depends_on": [],
      "group": "Booking API"
    },
    {
      "key": "b2",
      "title": "Add token authentication",
      "description": "Protect all booking endpoints with token‑based authentication.",
      "phase": "implement",
      "requirement_ids": ["R5"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Endpoints reject requests without a valid token with 401",
        "Endpoints accept requests with a valid token",
        "Invalid token returns 401"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 4,
      "depends_on": ["b1"],
      "group": "Security"
    },
    {
      "key": "b3",
      "title": "Ensure JSON responses and status codes",
      "description": "Make sure every endpoint returns JSON payloads and the correct HTTP status codes.",
      "phase": "implement",
      "requirement_ids": ["R4"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "All responses have Content‑Type: application/json",
        "Create returns 201, List returns 200, Cancel returns 204",
        "Error cases return appropriate 4xx codes with JSON error body"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 3,
      "depends_on": ["b1", "b2"],
      "group": "API Contract"
    },
    {
      "key": "t1",
      "title": "Test booking endpoint functionality",
      "description": "Write and run integration tests for create, list, and cancel operations.",
      "phase": "test",
      "requirement_ids": ["R3"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Create test passes when a booking is stored and 201 returned",
        "List test returns previously created bookings with 200",
        "Cancel test removes a booking and returns 204"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 4,
      "depends_on": ["b1", "b2", "b3"],
      "group": "Booking API"
    },
    {
      "key": "t2",
      "title": "Test authentication enforcement",
      "description": "Verify that endpoints reject unauthenticated requests and accept valid tokens.",
      "phase": "test",
      "requirement_ids": ["R5"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Requests without token receive 401",
        "Requests with valid token succeed",
        "Requests with invalid token receive 401"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 2,
      "depends_on": ["b2"],
      "group": "Security"
    },
    {
      "key": "t3",
      "title": "Test JSON format and status codes",
      "description": "Check that every response conforms to JSON format and uses the correct HTTP status.",
      "phase": "test",
      "requirement_ids": ["R4"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "All successful responses have JSON bodies",
        "Status codes match the specification for each endpoint",
        "Error responses include JSON error details"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 2,
      "depends_on": ["b3"],
      "group": "API Contract"
    }
  ],
  "research_questions": [
    "Which Python web framework (e.g., FastAPI vs Flask) best supports token authentication and schema validation for this project?",
    "What token scheme (JWT, simple bearer token, etc.) is allowed by the course constraints?",
    "How can the JSON schema from Part A be integrated for request validation in the chosen framework?",
    "Are there known concurrency issues with booking cancellation that need special handling?"
  ],
  "not_plannable": [],
  "open_questions": []
}
